Committee: Healthcare
Sponsor: Coleman-Madison
Analyst: Bryan Young
Date: 02/22/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 179 as introduced could increase the administrative obligations of the Alabama Board of Nursing by an undetermined amount to adopt rules establishing standards for student nurse apprenticeships and certified medication assistants, and the issuance of permits by the Board to eligible students and applicants. Any increase in obligation would be offset, wholly or partly, by the issuance of student nurse apprenticeship permits and certified medication assistants, permits and the amounts set by the Board.
Jim McClendon, Chairperson

Committee: Health
Sponsor: Coleman-Madison
Analyst: Bryan Young
Date: 03/05/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 179 as passed the Senate could increase the administrative obligations of the Alabama Board of Nursing by an undetermined amount to adopt rules establishing standards for student nurse apprenticeships and certified medication assistants and issue permits to eligible students and applicants. Any increase in obligation would be offset, wholly or in part, by the collection of fees, set by the Board, for student nurse apprenticeship permits and certified medication assistants.
Paul W. Lee, Chair

Committee: Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry
Sponsor: Allen
Analyst: John Friedenreich
Date: 03/31/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 460 as amended and reported by the Committee on Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry would (1) remove the four license plate limit on the reduced annual license tax and registration fee, ($250) for farm truck tractors; and (2) provide that the current annual license tax and registration fees for truck and truck-tractors are applicable to forest product trucks weighing over 42,000 pounds gross vehicle weight that transport forest products from point of severance to a sawmill or papermill.
This bill could reduce receipts to the Public Road and Bridge Fund, the several counties, and the several municipalities by an undetermined amount dependent on the number of additional farm truck license plates issued for truck tractors that exceed 42,000 pounds and are owned and used by farmers transporting farm products. For each additional farm license plate issued using the reduced rates under the provisions of this bill, the annual license tax and registration fee would be decreased by a minimum of $335 to a maximum of $640 per license plate, dependent upon the weight of the truck or truck tractor.
Larry Stutts, Chairperson
Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry
